name: Haggai

objectives.text: Identify Haggai as a prophet God sent to His people after they came home from exile to tell them to rebuild the temple
Retell how the people built their own houses while God's house stayed in ruins
Recall the promise "I am with you" that God gave the builders through Haggai
Explain what Haggai meant when he told the people to "consider your ways"
Describe how Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people responded to Haggai's message by obeying and returning to work on the temple
Explain how the drought and poor harvests in Haggai show that God rules over rain, crops, and all creation
Explain why some of the people were discouraged when they compared the new temple with Solomon's temple and how God answered their discouragement
Explain from Haggai the tradition's teaching that God's Spirit stirs up and strengthens His people to do the work He gives them
Identify the four dated messages in Haggai and summarize the main point of each
Construct a timeline of the post-exilic period that places Haggai's messages among the events recorded in Ezra, including the return, the halted work, and the temple's completion
Analyze how Haggai connects the people's neglect and obedience with curse and blessing in light of the covenant warnings of Deuteronomy
Explain the priestly ruling about holy and unclean things in Haggai 2 and how Haggai applied it to the people's offerings
Interpret the promise that the latter glory of the temple will be greater than the former in light of Christ's coming as God's presence with His people
Analyze how Hebrews interprets Haggai's prophecy of the shaking of the heavens and the earth as pointing to an unshakable kingdom
Analyze Haggai's literary features, including its dated oracles and repeated calls to "consider" and "be strong", to show how they shape its message
Evaluate the messianic significance of the signet ring promise to Zerubbabel by comparing it with the judgment on Jehoiachin and its fulfillment in Christ the Son of David
Evaluate how the New Testament develops Haggai's temple theme into the teaching that the church is God's temple, as the Reformed tradition confesses about the visible church
Evaluate how Haggai's call to put God's house first addresses neglect of worship and the work of the church among God's people today
Create an expository outline of one of Haggai's messages that explains its historical setting, its main point, and its fulfillment in Christ

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies: Haggai as post-exilic prophet, neglected temple versus own houses, consider your ways, discouragement over the smaller temple, obedience and blessing (now framed through Deuteronomy's covenant warnings), latter glory, the shaking (tied to Hebrews 12), the post-exilic timeline with Ezra (absorbing Zerubbabel and Joshua), and the signet ring (tied to Jeremiah 22 and Matthew 1). Dropped vague or affective filler (God wants to be first, apply the lesson) and the bare defense of the visible church, which became an evaluation of the NT temple theme anchored in WCF 25.2. Replaced the apathy essay with an evaluation of neglect of worship and an expository outline task. Added missing content: the people's obedient response, the I am with you promise, God's rule over drought (HC Q27, WCF 5.1), the Spirit enabling the work (WCF 16.3), the four dated messages, the holy and unclean ruling of Haggai 2, and the book's literary structure. Replaced whole-verse citations with specific passages.
